messages:
joel: quick heads upwe're scheduling a small planned window to validate an nvme driver microfix + controlled reboots. target: 03:30-04:30 UTC tonight. scope: 9 GPU hosts in az3 (gpu-pool-c[32-40]). goal: reproduce the occasional blk-mq stalls and confirm the kernel param tweak fixes IO stalls without impacting scheduling. rolling batches of 3 hosts.

tariq: what's the exact impact surface? reserved/dedicated customers?

joel: this only touches interruptible and spot backfill pools. Dedicated customers remain on separate racks. still could observe transient queueing on egress paths if backfill shifts.

sophia: capacity check? our last telemetry spike was during peak work hours in APAC, want to avoid overlap.

joel: agreedwe picked 03:30 UTC to avoid apac spike. cluster-sim shows ~22% cushion across regions after shifting noncritical jobs. backfill plan: hot-standby hosts in az3 and az1, pre-warm prefix cache, and temporarily raise scoring weight for warm racks.

ryan: can you paste the commands/playbook steps so we can review taints/eviction timeouts?

joel: playbook snippet: `kubectl cordon <node>` -> `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --grace-period=120 --delete-local-data` -> ssh & `sudo modprobe -r nvme && sudo modprobe nvme && sudo reboot` -> post-reboot: run kv prewarm and `infra-trace --collect dmesg,syslog -o /tmp/trace-<node>.tgz`. if `cache.prefix.ready` not seen in 2m, open rollback.

tariq: 2m seems tight for some big caches. can we increase to 4m and gate on 95th percentile seed time?

joel: ok bump gate to 4m and require `cache.prefix.ok` metric. if two consecutive nodes exceed gate we pause the window and notify infra-oncall.

ops-bot: scheduled by joel: az3-nvme-hotpatch @ 2026-04-02T03:30:00Z -> 2026-04-02T04:30:00Z. Runbook: https://go/runbooks/infra/az3-nvme-hotpatch. Pager duty: infra-oncall.

ryan: customer comms needed? I'd suggest a short line for #customers-alerts: "We expect no service interruption for Dedicated customers. Intermittent pools may see brief scheduling delays while we validate an NVMe driver fix."

joel: fine, please post that 45m before start. also add a note for #support-ops to watch `gpu.latency.p50/p95` and `nvme.latency.ms` dashboards.

sophia: can we enable lightweight BPF probe for the batch? capture only nvme submit/complete events to minimize overhead.

joel: yestracing step added: `bpftrace -e 'tracepoint:block:block_rq_issue /comm=="kworker/"/ { @[comm] = hist(nsecs_to_ms(args->nr_sectors)) }' -o /tmp/bpf-<node>.txt` (saved compressed). keep CPU overhead <2%.

tariq: cost estimate? shifting jobs to warm racks may bump reserved GPU-hours accounting if we hold backfill for longer.

joel: preliminary estimate ~0.4% extra GPU-hours for the hour window; ops finance okayed it. wrote numbers in runbook.

ryan: I'll be on standby for rollout. who is executing?

joel: me + tariq will execute. ryan you'll monitor dashboards and support comms. ops-bot will post start/complete events.

ops-bot: joel started maintenance: az3-nvme-hotpatch at 2026-04-02T03:30:00Z (this is a scheduled placeholder message).

joel: kicking cohort 1 (nodes c32-c34) in ~5m. leaving thread open for live notes.
